name: Cosmo Monkhouse
credit: Portrait of Cosmo Monkhouse by John McLure Hamilton · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: William Cosmo Monkhouse (1840–1901) was a British poet and critic.

The poems here are taken from Alfred H. Miles (ed.), The Poets and the Poetry of the Century (London: Hutchinson, 1891–1897), vol. 6, from the Internet Archive scans of that edition. Spelling is that of the anthology; Miles's biographical essay and extracts from longer poems are omitted, and only poems that could be read cleanly from the scan are included.

poems.title: A Song of the Seasons
poems.author: Cosmo Monkhouse
poems.text:
Sing a song of Spring-time,
The world is going round,
Blown by the south wind:
Listen to its sound.
" Gurgle " goes the mill-wheel,
"Cluck "clucks the hen;
And it's O for a pretty girl
To kiss in the glen.

Sing a song of Summer,
The world is nearly still,
The mill-pool has gone to sleep,
And so has the mill.
Shall we go a-sailing,
Or shall we take a ride.
Or dream the afternoon away
Here, side by side?

Sing a song of Autumn,
The world is going back;
They glean in the corn-field.
And stamp on the stack.
Our boy, Charlie,
Tall, strong, and light:
He shoots all the day
And dances all night.

Sing a song of Winter,
The world stops dead;
Under snowy coverlid
Flowers lie a-bed.
There's hunting for the young ones
And wine for the old,
And a sexton in the churchyard
Digging in the cold.

poems.title: Sonnet: To the Sea
poems.author: Cosmo Monkhouse
poems.text:
O senseless Sea, how long shall men proclaim
Thy freedom and thy power! Slave of the Moon,
Thy wrath is borrowed of the wind, the Noon
Supplies thy smiles, thy life is but a name
That poets use. To thee nor praise nor blame
Belongs. And yet shall man, alas, not soon
Forget to fear thee, and thy dim halls strewn
With bones of bravest man and fairest dame.
The careless fish within thee sport and breed,
The bird above thee spreads her scornful wing:
Yet thou, more lifeless than thy weakest weed,
Canst shake the very soul of Priest and King.
And aye to man thy breathless breast appears
A waste of sighs, a wilderness of tears.

poems.title: Rondeau: Violet
poems.author: Cosmo Monkhouse
poems.text:
Violet, delicate, sweet,
Down in the deep of the wood,
Hid in thy still retreat,
Far from the sound of the street,

Man and his merciless mood: —
Safe from the storm and the heat.
Breathing of beauty and good
Fragrantly under thy hood,
Violet.
Beautiful maid, discreet,
Where is the mate that is meet,

Meet for thee — strive as he could!
Yet will I kneel at thy feet,
Fearing another one should,
Violet!
